heterodontosaurus:eswiki:9.title: Heterodontosaurus tucki (El crecimiento y la ontogenia)

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic period, approximately 200 to 190 million years ago.
facts.quote: Heterodontosaurus is a genus of heterodontosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Early Jurassic, 200–190 million years ago.

facts.statement: The species Heterodontosaurus tucki was named in 1962 based on a skull found in South Africa.
facts.quote: Its only known member species, Heterodontosaurus tucki, was named in 1962 based on a skull discovered in South Africa.

facts.statement: An almost complete skeleton of Heterodontosaurus was discovered in 1966.
facts.quote: Further specimens have since been found, including an almost complete skeleton in 1966.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus was a small dinosaur that grew between 1.18 and 1.75 meters long and weighed between 2 and 10 kilograms.
facts.quote: Though it was a small dinosaur, Heterodontosaurus was one of the largest members of its family, reaching between 1.18 m and possibly 1.75 m in length, and weighing between 2 and 10 kg.

facts.statement: The skull of Heterodontosaurus was elongated, narrow, and triangular in side view.
facts.quote: The skull was elongated, narrow, and triangular when viewed from the side.

facts.statement: The front of Heterodontosaurus jaws was covered by a horny beak.
facts.quote: The front of the jaws were covered in a horny beak.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus possessed three types of teeth: small incisor-like teeth, long canine-like tusks, and chisel-like cheek teeth separated by a gap.
facts.quote: It had three types of teeth; in the upper jaw, small, incisor-like teeth were followed by long, canine-like tusks. A gap divided the tusks from the chisel-like cheek-teeth.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had a short body and a long tail.
facts.quote: The body was short with a long tail.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had long, robust five-fingered forelimbs and long, slender hindlimbs with four toes.
facts.quote: The five-fingered forelimbs were long and relatively robust, whereas the hind-limbs were long, slender, and had four toes.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus is now considered to have been bipedal, although it was previously thought to be capable of quadrupedal movement.
facts.quote: Though it was formerly thought to have been capable of quadrupedal locomotion, it is now thought to have been bipedal.

facts.statement: Unlike its relatives, Heterodontosaurus experienced sporadic rather than continuous tooth replacement.
facts.quote: Tooth replacement was sporadic and not continuous, unlike its relatives.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Heterodontosaurus tucki was discovered during a British-South African expedition in 1961–1962.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Heterodontosaurus tucki (SAM-PK-K337) was discovered during the British–South African expedition to South Africa and Basutoland (former name of Lesotho) in 1961–1962.

facts.statement: The holotype was excavated at an altitude of about 1890 meters at the Tyinindini locality in the Cape Province of South Africa.
facts.quote: It was excavated on a mountain at an altitude of about 1890 m, at a locality called Tyinindini, in the district of Transkei (sometimes referred to as Herschel) in the Cape Province of South Africa.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus was scientifically described and named in 1962 by Alfred Walter Crompton and Alan J. Charig.
facts.quote: The animal was scientifically described and named in 1962 by palaeontologists Alfred Walter Crompton and Alan J. Charig.

facts.statement: The genus name refers to the animal's different-shaped teeth, while the species name honors George C. Tuck, who supported the expedition.
facts.quote: The genus name refers to the different-shaped teeth, and the specific name honors George C. Tuck, a director of Austin Motor Company, who supported the expedition.

facts.statement: A second specimen was discovered in 1966 at the Voyizane locality in the Elliot Formation, 1,770 meters above sea level on Krommespruit Mountain.
facts.quote: In 1966, a second specimen of Heterodontosaurus (SAM-PK-K1332) was discovered at the Voyizane locality, in the Elliot Formation of the Stormberg Group of rock formations, 1,770 m above sea level, on Krommespruit Mountain.

facts.statement: The second specimen preserved the skull and skeleton in articulation with little displacement or distortion.
facts.quote: This specimen included both the skull and skeleton, preserved in articulation (i.e. the bones being preserved in their natural position in relation to each other), with little displacement and distortion of the bones.

facts.statement: The skull of Heterodontosaurus was not fully described until 2011 by David B. Norman and colleagues.
facts.quote: It was not until 2011 that the skull was fully described by the palaeontologist David B. Norman and colleagues.

facts.statement: A very complete specimen was found in 2005 near Grahamstown in the Eastern Cape Province, though the surrounding rocks were too hard to remove fully.
facts.quote: In 2005, a new Heterodontosaurus specimen (AM 4766) was found in a streambed near Grahamstown in the Eastern Cape Province; it was very complete, but the rocks around it were too hard to fully remove.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus is the namesake and best-known member of the family Heterodontosauridae.
facts.quote: Heterodontosaurus is the eponymous and best-known member of the family Heterodontosauridae.

facts.statement: In 1970, Richard A. Thulborn suggested that Heterodontosaurus was a junior synonym of the genus Lycorhinus.
facts.quote: In 1970, palaeontologist Richard A. Thulborn suggested that Heterodontosaurus was a junior synonym of the genus Lycorhinus, which was named in 1924 with the species L. angustidens, also from a specimen discovered in South Africa.

facts.statement: In 1974, Charig and Crompton agreed that Heterodontosaurus and Lycorhinus belonged to the same family but disagreed on whether they were similar enough to be in the same genus.
facts.quote: In 1974, Charig and Crompton agreed that Heterodontosaurus and Lycorhinus belonged in the same family, Heterodontosauridae, but disagreed that they were similar enough to be considered congeneric.

facts.statement: The most complete skeleton of Heterodontosaurus measured approximately 1.18 meters in length.
facts.quote: The most complete skeleton, SAM-PK-K1332, belonged to an animal measuring about 1.18 m in length.

facts.statement: Studies have estimated the weight of Heterodontosaurus at 1.8 kg, 2.59 kg, and 3.4 kg.
facts.quote: Its weight was variously estimated at 1.8 kg, 2.59 kg, and 3.4 kg in separate studies.

facts.statement: An incomplete skull specimen suggests Heterodontosaurus could have reached a length of 1.75 meters and a mass of nearly 10 kilograms.
facts.quote: A second specimen, consisting of an incomplete skull, indicates that Heterodontosaurus could have grown substantially larger – up to a length of 1.75 m and with a body mass of nearly 10 kg.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus is often compared in size to a turkey.
facts.quote: The size of this dinosaur has been compared to that of a turkey.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Paul Sereno suggested that Heterodontosaurus may have resembled a nimble, two-legged porcupine.
facts.quote: Sereno has stated that a heterodontosaur may have looked like a "nimble two-legged porcupine" in life.

facts.statement: A restoration by Paul Sereno includes a hypothetical display structure on the snout above the nasal fossa.
facts.quote: The restoration published by Sereno also featured a hypothetical display structure located on the snout, above the nasal fossa (depression).

facts.statement: The two most complete skulls of Heterodontosaurus measured 108 mm and 121 mm in length.
facts.quote: The two most complete skulls measured 108 mm (holotype specimen SAM-PK-K337) and 121 mm (specimen SAM-PK-K1332) in length.

facts.statement: The skull was elongated, narrow, and triangular, sloping down from the sagittal crest to the snout tip.
facts.quote: The skull was elongated, narrow, and triangular when viewed from the side, with the highest point being the sagittal crest, from where the skull sloped down towards the snout tip.

facts.statement: A horn-like structure projected sideways from the jugal bone below the eye socket.
facts.quote: Below the eye socket, the jugal bone gave rise to a sideways projecting boss, or horn-like structure.

facts.statement: The front of the jaws was covered by a toothless keratinous beak.
facts.quote: The front of the jaws were covered by a toothless keratinous beak (or rhamphotheca).

facts.statement: The upper canines had fine serrations on the back edge, while the lower canines were serrated at the front.
facts.quote: The canines had fine serrations along the back edge, but only the lower ones were serrated at the front.

facts.statement: Eleven tall, chisel-like cheek-teeth lined each side of the upper jaw, separated from the canines by a large gap.
facts.quote: Eleven tall and chisel-like cheek-teeth lined each side of the posterior parts of the upper jaw, which were separated from the canines by a large diastema (gap).

facts.statement: The inset upper and lower teeth rows created a cheek-recess similar to other ornithischians.
facts.quote: The upper and lower teeth rows were inset, which created a "cheek-recess" also seen in other ornithischians.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Heterodontosaurus may have had lip-like structures rather than bridging skin between the jaws.
facts.quote: It has also been suggested that heterodontosaurs and other basal (or "primitive") orhithischians had lip-like structures like lizards do (based on similarities in their jaws), rather than bridging skin between the upper and lower jaws (such as cheeks).

facts.statement: The function of the nasal fossa or sulcus above the snout is unknown.
facts.quote: A depression above the snout has been termed the "nasal fossa" or "sulcus". A similar fossa is also seen in Tianyulong, Agilisaurus, and Eoraptor, but its function is unknown.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had a neck made of nine vertebrae that formed an S-shaped curve.
facts.quote: The neck consisted of nine cervical vertebrae, which would have formed an S-shaped curve, as indicated by the shape of the vertebral bodies in the side view of the skeleton.

facts.statement: The tail of Heterodontosaurus was long relative to its body and likely contained between 34 and 37 vertebrae.
facts.quote: The tail was long compared to the body; although incompletely known, it probably consisted of 34 to 37 caudal vertebrae.

facts.statement: Ossified tendons stiffened the dorsal spine of Heterodontosaurus starting from the fourth vertebra.
facts.quote: The dorsal spine was stiffened by ossified tendons, beginning with the fourth dorsal vertebra.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus possessed a suprascapula bone on its shoulder blade, a feature otherwise known only in the dinosaur Parksosaurus.
facts.quote: The shoulder blade was capped by an additional element, the suprascapula, which is, among dinosaurs, otherwise only known from Parksosaurus.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus is the only known ornithischian dinosaur that possessed gastralia, bony elements located within the skin.
facts.quote: Heterodontosaurus is the only known ornithischian that possessed gastralia (bony elements within the skin between the sternal plates and the pubis of the pelvis).

facts.statement: The gastralia of Heterodontosaurus were arranged in two rows, with each row containing approximately nine elements.
facts.quote: The gastralia were arranged in two lengthwise rows, each containing around nine elements.

facts.statement: The forelimbs of Heterodontosaurus were robust and measured 70% of the length of its hind limbs.
facts.quote: The forelimbs were robustly built and proportionally long, measuring 70% of the length of the hind limbs.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had a large hand nearly as long as its upper arm bone, equipped with five grasping fingers.
facts.quote: The hand was large, approaching the humerus in length, and possessed five fingers equipped for grasping.

facts.statement: The first three fingers of Heterodontosaurus ended in large and strong claws.
facts.quote: The first three fingers ended in large and strong claws.

facts.statement: The finger bone arrangement of Heterodontosaurus followed the formula 2-3-4-3-2.
facts.quote: The phalangeal formula, which states the number of finger bones in each finger starting from the first, was 2-3-4-3-2.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had long, slender hindlimbs ending in four toes, with the first toe not touching the ground.
facts.quote: The hindlimbs were long, slender, and ended in four toes, the first of which (the hallux) did not contact the ground.

facts.statement: Uniquely among ornithischians, Heterodontosaurus had fused leg and foot bones, including a tibiotarsus and a tarsometatarsus.
facts.quote: Uniquely for ornithischians, several bones of the leg and foot were fused: the tibia and fibula were fused with upper tarsal bones (astragalus and calcaneus), forming a tibiotarsus, while the lower tarsal bones were fused with the metatarsal bones, forming a tarsometatarsus.

facts.statement: The tibiotarsus of Heterodontosaurus was approximately 30% longer than its femur.
facts.quote: The tibiotarsus was about 30% longer than the femur.

facts.statement: The toe bones of Heterodontosaurus were claw-like rather than hoof-like like those of more advanced ornithischians.
facts.quote: The ungual bones of the toes were claw-like, and not hoof-like as in more advanced ornithischians.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus was first described in 1962 as a primitive member of the order Ornithischia.
facts.quote: When it was described in 1962, Heterodontosaurus was classified as a primitive member of Ornithischia, one of the two main orders of Dinosauria (the other being Saurischia).

facts.statement: The family Heterodontosauridae was named in 1966 by Alfred Romer and Oskar Kuhn to include Heterodontosaurus and Lycorhinus.
facts.quote: The palaeontologists Alfred Romer and Oskar Kuhn independently named the family Heterodontosauridae in 1966 as a family of ornithischian dinosaurs including Heterodontosaurus and Lycorhinus.

facts.statement: Sereno defined Heterodontosauridae as a clade in 1998 and 2005 based on skull features like few premaxillary teeth, caniniform teeth, and a jugal horn.
facts.quote: Heterodontosauridae was defined as a clade by Sereno in 1998 and 2005, and the group shares skull features such as three or fewer teeth in each premaxilla, caniniform teeth followed by a diastema, and a jugal horn below the eye.

facts.statement: In 2006, Xu Xing and colleagues named the clade Heterodontosauriformes to include Heterodontosauridae and Marginocephalia.
facts.quote: In 2006, palaeontologist Xu Xing and colleagues named the clade Heterodontosauriformes, which included Heterodontosauridae and Marginocephalia, since some features earlier only known from heterodontosaurs were also seen in the basal ceratopsian genus Yinlong.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurids existed from the Late Triassic to the Early Cretaceous, spanning at least 100 million years.
facts.quote: Heterodontosaurids persisted from the Late Triassic until the Early Cretaceous period, and existed for at least a 100 million years.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurids are known from Africa, Eurasia, and the Americas, with most fossils found in southern Africa.
facts.quote: They are known from Africa, Eurasia, and the Americas, but the majority have been found in southern Africa.

facts.statement: The unique teeth and jaws of heterodontosaurines were specialized for processing plant material with a sophistication comparable to later ornithischians.
facts.quote: The unique tooth and jaw features of heterodontosaurines appear to be specialisations for effectively processing plant material, and their level of sophistication is comparable to that of later ornithischians.

facts.statement: In 2017, Matthew G. Baron and colleagues suggested grouping ornithischians with theropods in Ornithoscelida based on similarities between Heterodontosaurus and Eoraptor.
facts.quote: In 2017, similarities between the skeletons of Heterodontosaurus and the early theropod Eoraptor were used by palaeontologist Matthew G. Baron and colleagues to suggest that ornithischians should be grouped with theropods in a group called Ornithoscelida.

facts.statement: In 2020, Paul-Emile Dieudonné and colleagues proposed that Heterodontosauridae were basal members of Pachycephalosauria rather than a distinct natural group.
facts.quote: In 2020, palaeontologist Paul-Emile Dieudonné and colleagues suggested that members of Heterodontosauridae were basal marginocephalians not forming their own natural group, instead progressively leading to Pachycephalosauria, and were therefore basal members of that group.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus is commonly considered a herbivorous dinosaur.
facts.quote: Heterodontosaurus is commonly regarded as a herbivorous dinosaur.

facts.statement: In 1974, Thulborn suggested the tusks were likely used for combat, display, or defense rather than feeding.
facts.quote: In 1974, Thulborn proposed that the tusks of the dinosaur played no important role in feeding; rather, that they would have been used in combat with conspecifics, for display, as a visual threat, or for active defence.

facts.statement: In 2000, Paul Barrett proposed that Heterodontosaurus may have been an occasional carnivore based on its tooth shape and serrated tusks.
facts.quote: In 2000, Paul Barrett suggested that the shape of the premaxillary teeth and the fine serration of the tusks are reminiscent of carnivorous animals, hinting at facultative carnivory.

facts.statement: In 2008, Butler and colleagues argued that the tusks grew early in development and thus were not a sign of sexual dimorphism.
facts.quote: In 2008, Butler and colleagues argued that the enlarged tusks formed early in the development of the individual, and therefore could not constitute sexual dimorphism.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus possessed long arms with large, curved claws that could help it seize small prey.
facts.quote: In 2011, Norman and colleagues drew attention to the arms and hands, which are relatively long and equipped with large, recurved claws.

facts.statement: If an omnivore, Heterodontosaurus would have had an advantage during dry seasons when plant food was scarce.
facts.quote: As an omnivore, Heterodontosaurus would have had a significant selection advantage during the dry season when vegetation was scarce.

facts.statement: In 2012, Sereno argued that skull and tooth features indicate Heterodontosaurus was primarily or exclusively herbivorous.
facts.quote: In 2012, Sereno pointed out several skull and dentition features that suggest a purely or at least preponderantly herbivorous diet.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had enlarged jaw muscles and a jaw joint positioned below the teeth to allow for an even bite along the tooth row.
facts.quote: The jaw muscles were enlarged, and the jaw joint was set below the level of the teeth.

facts.statement: A 2016 study found the bite force of Heterodontosaurus was comparable to that of the dinosaur Scelidosaurus.
facts.quote: A 2016 study of ornithischian jaw mechanics found that the relative bite forces of Heterodontosaurus was comparable to that of the more derived Scelidosaurus.

facts.statement: Butler and colleagues suggested Heterodontosaurus specialized in tough plants, while later relatives likely had a more generalized diet including invertebrates.
facts.quote: Butler and colleagues suggested that the feeding apparatus of Heterodontosaurus was specialised to process tough plant material, and that late-surviving members of the family (Fruitadens, Tianyulong and Echinodon) probably showed a more generalised diet including both plants and invertebrates.

facts.statement: There is significant controversy regarding whether Heterodontosaurus exhibited continuous tooth replacement like other dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Much controversy has surrounded the question of whether or not, and to what degree, Heterodontosaurus showed the continuous tooth replacement that is typical for other dinosaurs and reptiles.

facts.statement: In 1974 and 1978, Thulborn found no evidence of continuous tooth replacement in known skulls, suggesting teeth formed simultaneously.
facts.quote: In 1974 and 1978, Thulborn found that the skulls known at that time lacked any indications of continuous tooth replacement: The cheek teeth of the known skulls are worn uniformly, indicating that they formed simultaneously.

facts.statement: Thulborn hypothesized that complete tooth replacement occurred only during aestivation, a period when the animal did not feed.
facts.quote: Such a complete replacement could only have been possible within phases of aestivation, when the animal did not feed.

facts.statement: Thulborn's aestivation hypothesis fits the supposed desert-like habitat of Heterodontosaurus with its hot, dry seasons.
facts.quote: Aestivation also complies with the supposed habitat of the animals, which would have been desert-like, including hot dry seasons when food was scarce.

facts.statement: Hopson demonstrated variable tooth wear, suggesting continuous tooth replacement occurred in Heterodontosaurus.
facts.quote: Furthermore, Hopson demonstrated variability in the degree of tooth wear, indicating continuous tooth replacement.

facts.statement: Hopson rejected Thulborn's aestivation hypothesis because there was insufficient evidence to support it.
facts.quote: Thulborn's aestivation hypothesis was rejected by Hopson due to lack of evidence.

facts.statement: In 2006, Butler and colleagues used CT scans on juvenile skull SAM-PK-K10487 to study tooth development.
facts.quote: In 2006, Butler and colleagues conducted computer tomography scans of the juvenile skull SAM-PK-K10487.

facts.statement: Surprisingly, Butler and colleagues found unerupted replacement teeth in a juvenile skull, indicating early tooth replacement.
facts.quote: To the surprise of these researchers, replacement teeth yet to erupt were present even in this early ontogenetic stage.

facts.statement: Butler and colleagues concluded that tooth replacement in Heterodontosaurus was more sporadic than in related dinosaurs.
facts.quote: In conclusion, Butler and colleagues suggested that tooth replacement in Heterodontosaurus must have been more sporadic than in related dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Unerupted replacement teeth were not found in Heterodontosaurus until 2011, when Norman and colleagues described specimen SAM-PK-K1334.
facts.quote: Unerupted replacement teeth in Heterodontosaurus were not discovered until 2011, when Norman and colleagues described the upper jaw of specimen SAM-PK-K1334.

facts.statement: A juvenile skull described by Sereno in 2012 also contained unerupted replacement teeth.
facts.quote: Another juvenile skull (AMNH 24000) described by Sereno in 2012 also yielded unerupted replacement teeth.

facts.statement: Discoveries show that tooth replacement in Heterodontosaurus was episodic rather than continuous like in other heterodontosaurids.
facts.quote: As shown by these discoveries, tooth replacement in Heterodontosaurus was episodical and not continuous as in other heterodontosaurids.

facts.statement: In 1980, Santa Luca described features of the forelimb implying strong arm musculature in Heterodontosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1980, Santa Luca described several features of the forelimb that are also present in recent quadrupedal animals and imply a strong arm musculature

facts.statement: Santa Luca proposed that Heterodontosaurus moved quadrupedally when slow but could switch to a faster bipedal run.
facts.quote: According to Santa Luca, Heterodontosaurus was quadrupedal when moving slowly but was able to switch to a much faster, bipedal run

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the robust arms of Heterodontosaurus were adapted for foraging, possibly by digging up roots and breaking insect nests.
facts.quote: The anatomical evidence suggested by Santa Luca was identified as adaptations for foraging; the robust and strong arms might have been used for digging up roots and breaking open insect nests

facts.statement: A 2009 study by Herman Pontzer and colleagues indicated Heterodontosaurus was endothermic because its aerobic endurance exceeded that of cold-blooded animals.
facts.quote: In a 2009 study, Herman Pontzer and colleagues calculated the aerobic endurance of various dinosaurs. Even at moderate running speeds, Heterodontosaurus would have exceeded the maximum aerobic capabilities possible for an ectotherm (cold-blooded) animal, indicating endothermy in this genus

facts.statement: In 2021, Viktor Radermacher and colleagues argued based on specimen AM 4766 that the breathing system of ornithischians like Heterodontosaurus differed drastically from other dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Based on synchrotron data of a well-preserved Heterodontosaurus specimen (AM 4766), Viktor Radermacher and colleagues, in 2021, argued that the breathing system of ornithischians drastically differed from that of other dinosaurs

facts.statement: A juvenile Heterodontosaurus skull measured 45 mm, suggesting a total body length of 450 mm if adult proportions applied.
facts.quote: The length of the juvenile skull was suggested to be 45 mm. Assuming similar body proportions as adult individuals, the body length of this juvenile would have been 450 mm

facts.statement: In 1974, Thulborn hypothesized that large tusks in heterodontosaurids were secondary sex characteristics present only in adult males.
facts.quote: In 1974, Thulborn suggested that the large tusks of heterodontosaurids represented a secondary sex characteristic. According to this theory, only adult male individuals would have possessed fully developed tusks

facts.statement: In 2006, Richard Butler and colleagues questioned the sexual dimorphism hypothesis, noting that a juvenile skull possessed tusks.
facts.quote: This hypothesis was questioned by palaeontologist Richard Butler and colleagues in 2006, who argued that the juvenile skull SAM-PK-K10487 possessed tusks despite its early developmental state

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus fossils are found in the Upper Elliot and Clarens Formations of the Karoo Supergroup, dating to the Lower Jurassic (Hettangian and Sinemurian ages) around 200–190 million years ago.
facts.quote: Heterodontosaurus is known from fossils found in formations of the Karoo Supergroup, including the Upper Elliot Formation and the Clarens Formation, which date to the Hettangian and Sinemurian ages of the Lower Jurassic, around 200–190 million years ago

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus was originally thought to be from the Upper Triassic period before being re-dated to the Jurassic.
facts.quote: Originally, Heterodontosaurus was thought to be from the Upper Triassic period

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Heterodontosaurus specialized in tough plant material due to its dentition, while the related Abrictosaurus likely ate softer vegetation.
facts.quote: With its highly specialised dentition, Heterodontosaurus might have been specialised for tough plant material, while the less specialised Abrictosaurus might have predominantly consumed softer vegetation

facts.statement: The genus Heterodontosaurus was named by Charning and Crompton in 1962.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Charning & Crompton 1962

facts.statement: The species Heterodontosaurus tucki was named by Charning and Crompton in 1962.
facts.quote: species_authority: Charning & Crompton 1962

facts.statement: Lycorhinus tucki is a synonym for Heterodontosaurus tucki, originally described by Thulborn in 1970.
facts.quote: synonyms: Lycorhinus tucki Thulborn, 1970

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic period, approximately 200 to 190 million years ago, in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: Heterodontosaurus tucki es la única especie conocida del género extinto Heterodontosaurus (gr. "lagarto de dientes diferentes") de dinosaurio neornitisquio heterodontosáurido que vivió a principios del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 200 a 190 millones de años, en el Sinemuriano, en lo que hoy es África.

facts.statement: Paleontologists Alan Charig and Alfred Crompton discovered the remains of Heterodontosaurus in the 1960s in a mountainous area of South Africa.
facts.quote: En la década de 1960, los paleontólogos Alan Charning y Alfred Crompton descubrieron en un escarpado montañoso de Sudáfrica los restos de éste pequeño dinosaurio.

facts.statement: The fossils of Heterodontosaurus were found in the Upper Elliot Formation and the Clarence Formation.
facts.quote: Sus restos se encontraron en la Formación Elliot Superior y la Formación Clarence.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus was a small dinosaur that grew between 1.20 and possibly 1.75 meters long and weighed between 2 and 10 kilograms.
facts.quote: Aunque era un dinosaurio pequeño, Heterodontosaurus era uno de los miembros más grandes de su familia, alcanzaba entre 1,20 metros y posiblemente 1,75 metros de longitud y pesaba entre 2 y 10 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had long, relatively robust five-fingered forelimbs and long, thin four-fingered hindlimbs.
facts.quote: Las extremidades anteriores de cinco dedos eran largas y relativamente robustas, mientras que las extremidades posteriores eran largas, delgadas y tenían cuatro dedos.

facts.statement: The skull of Heterodontosaurus was elongated, narrow, and triangular when viewed from the side.
facts.quote: El cráneo era alargado, estrecho y triangular cuando se veía desde el lado.

facts.statement: The front of the jaws of Heterodontosaurus was covered by a horny beak.
facts.quote: La parte frontal de las mandíbulas estaba cubierta por un pico córneo.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had three types of teeth in its upper jaw: small incisor-like teeth followed by long canine-like fangs.
facts.quote: Tenía tres tipos de dientes, en la mandíbula superior, los dientes pequeños, como incisivos, seguidos por largos colmillos, como caninos.

facts.statement: A gap separated the fangs from the chisel-shaped teeth in Heterodontosaurus.
facts.quote: Una brecha dividía los colmillos de los dientes con forma de cincel.

facts.statement: While previously thought to be quadrupedal, Heterodontosaurus is now believed to have been bipedal.
facts.quote: Aunque antes se pensaba que era capaz de una locomoción cuadrúpeda, ahora se cree que fue bípedo.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had sporadic, non-continuous tooth replacement, unlike its relatives.
facts.quote: El reemplazo dental fue esporádico y no continuo, a diferencia de sus parientes.

facts.statement: The most complete skeleton of Heterodontosaurus, SAM-PK-K1332, belonged to an animal measuring approximately 1.18 meters in length.
facts.quote: El esqueleto más completo, SAM-PK-K1332, pertenecía a un animal que medía aproximadamente 1.18 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: The weight of the most complete Heterodontosaurus specimen was estimated to vary between 1.8, 2.59, and 3.4 kilograms in separate studies.
facts.quote: Su peso se estimó de manera diversa variando entre 1,8 kilogramos, 2,59 kilogramos y 3.4 kilogramos en estudios separados.

facts.statement: A second specimen with an incomplete skull suggests Heterodontosaurus could have grown up to 1.75 meters long and nearly 10 kilograms in mass.
facts.quote: Un segundo espécimen, que consiste en un cráneo incompleto, indica que Heterodontosaurus podría haber crecido sustancialmente más grande, hasta una longitud de 1,75 m y con una masa corporal de casi 10 kilogramos.

facts.statement: The size of Heterodontosaurus has been compared to that of a turkey.
facts.quote: El tamaño de este dinosaurio ha sido comparado con el de un pavo.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus teeth came in three forms: small and sharp, long and curved canine-like teeth possibly present only in males, and molariform or molar teeth.
facts.quote: Los dientes de Heterodontosaurus presentaban tres formas diferentes, los pequeños y afilados, los largos y curvos caniniformes, posiblemente sólo presentes en los machos y los molariformes o molares.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had a beak at the front of its jaw and small teeth behind it likely used for cutting leaves and shoots.
facts.quote: En el frente de la mandíbula tenía un pico y detrás pequeños dientes usados probablemente para cortar hojas y brotes.

facts.statement: The fused ankle structure of Heterodontosaurus resembles that of birds.
facts.quote: La estructura fusionada del tobillo hace recordar a la de las aves.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had tiny wrist bones, making the wrist functional and versatile, possibly used for grasping and pulling leaves.
facts.quote: Los huesos de sus muñecas eran diminutos, de ahí que la muñeca fuera funcional y versátil. Esta podría haber servido para agarrar y arrancar hojas.

facts.statement: Each hand of Heterodontosaurus had five fingers, two of which were opposable.
facts.quote: Cada mano tenía 5 dedos, dos de ellos oponibles.

facts.statement: The first three fingers of Heterodontosaurus ended in large, strong claws.
facts.quote: Los primeros tres dedos terminaron en garras grandes y fuertes.

facts.statement: The fourth and fifth fingers of Heterodontosaurus were strongly reduced and possibly vestigial.
facts.quote: Los dedos cuarto y quinto fueron fuertemente reducidos, y posiblemente vestigiales.

facts.statement: The phalangeal formula of Heterodontosaurus, indicating the number of finger bones from the first digit, is 2-3-4-3-2.
facts.quote: La fórmula falangeal, que indica el número de huesos de los dedos en cada dedo a partir del primero, es de 2-3-4-3-2.

facts.statement: The forelimbs of Heterodontosaurus were robust and proportionally long, measuring 70% of the length of the hindlimbs.
facts.quote: Las extremidades anteriores fueron construidas de manera robusta y proporcionalmente largas, midiendo el 70% de la longitud de las extremidades posteriores.

facts.statement: The radius of the forearm of Heterodontosaurus measured 70% of the length of the humerus.
facts.quote: El radio del antebrazo mide el 70% de la longitud del húmero, el hueso del antebrazo.

facts.statement: The hand of Heterodontosaurus was large, nearly as long as the humerus, and had five grasping fingers.
facts.quote: La mano era grande, se acercaba al húmero en longitud y tenía cinco dedos equipados para agarrar.

facts.statement: In Heterodontosaurus, the second finger was the longest, followed by the third and the first finger, the thumb.
facts.quote: El segundo dedo fue el más largo, seguido del tercero y el primer dedo, el pulgar.

facts.statement: The hind legs of Heterodontosaurus were long, thin, and ended in four toes, the first of which, the hallux, did not touch the ground.
facts.quote: Las patas traseras eran largas, delgadas y terminaban en cuatro dedos, el primero de los cuales, el hallux, no tocaba el suelo.

facts.statement: Unique among ornithischians, several leg and foot bones of Heterodontosaurus fused: the tibia and fibula fused with upper tarsal bones to form a tibiotarsus, while lower tarsal bones fused with metatarsals to form a tarsometatarsus.
facts.quote: Único para un ornitisquio, varios huesos de la pierna y el pie se fusionaron, la tibia y el peroné se fusionaron con los huesos del tarso superior, astrágalo y calcáneo , formando un tibiotarsos, mientras que los huesos del tarso inferior se fusionaron con los huesos metatarsianos, formando un tarsometatarsos.

facts.statement: The tibiotarsus of Heterodontosaurus was approximately 30% longer than the femur.
facts.quote: El tibiotarso era aproximadamente un 30% más largo que el fémur.

facts.statement: The ungual bones of the feet of Heterodontosaurus were like claws, not hooves like in more advanced ornithischians.
facts.quote: Los huesos unguales de los dedos de los pies eran como garras, y no como cascos como en oornitisquios más avanzados.

facts.statement: Paul Sereno has stated that a Heterodontosaurus may have looked like an "agile two-legged porcupine" in life.
facts.quote: Sereno ha declarado que un Heterodontosaurus puede haber parecido un " puercoespín ágil de dos patas" en la vida.

facts.statement: The restoration published by Sereno also presented a hypothetical display structure located on the snout, above the nasal fossa depression.
facts.quote: La restauración publicada por Sereno también presentó una estructura de exhibición hipotética ubicada en el hocico, sobre la depresión de la fosa nasal.

facts.statement: The neck of Heterodontosaurus consisted of 9 cervical vertebrae that would have formed an S-shaped curve.
facts.quote: El cuello consistía en 9 vértebras cervicales , que habrían formado una curva en forma de S, como lo indica la forma de los cuerpos vertebrales en la vista lateral del esqueleto.

facts.statement: The vertebral bodies of the anterior cervical vertebrae of Heterodontosaurus were parallelogram-shaped, the middle ones were rectangular, and the posterior ones were trapezoidal.
facts.quote: Los cuerpos vertebrales de las vértebras cervicales anteriores tienen forma de paralelogramo, las del medio son rectangulares y los de la parte posterior muestran una forma trapezoidal.

facts.statement: The trunk of Heterodontosaurus was short and consisted of 12 dorsal vertebrae and 6 fused sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: El tronco era corto y consistía de 12 vértebras dorsales y 6 sacras fusionadas.

facts.statement: The tail of Heterodontosaurus was long compared to the body and likely consisted of 34 to 37 caudal vertebrae, though known incompletely.
facts.quote: La cola era larga en comparación con el cuerpo, aunque se conoce de forma incompleta, probablemente consistía de 34 a 37 vértebras caudales.

facts.statement: The spine of Heterodontosaurus was rigid due to ossified tendons, starting from the fourth dorsal vertebra.
facts.quote: La espina dorsal estaba rígida por tendones osificados, comenzando por la cuarta vértebra dorsal.

facts.statement: This feature is present in many other ornithischian dinosaurs and likely counteracted stress caused by bending forces acting on the spine during bipedal locomotion.
facts.quote: Esta característica está presente en muchos otros dinosaurios ornitisquios y probablemente contrarrestó el estrés causado por las fuerzas de flexión que actúan sobre la columna vertebral durante la locomoción bípeda.

facts.statement: In contrast to many other ornithischians, the tail of Heterodontosaurus lacked ossified tendons and was therefore likely flexible.
facts.quote: En contraste con muchos otros ornitisquios, la cola de Heterodontosaurus carecía de tendones osificados, y por lo tanto era probablemente flexible.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus is the type and most well-known member of the family Heterodontosauridae.
facts.quote: Heterodontosaurus es el miembro que le da nombre y más conocido de la familia Heterodontosauridae.

facts.statement: Many paleontologists still consider Heterodontosaurus an ornithopod, although the theory of classifying it within ceratopsians is increasingly accepted.
facts.quote: Muchos paleontólogos aún consideran al Heterodontosaurus como un ornitópodo, aunque cada vez es más aceptada la teoría de clasificarlo dentro de los ceratopsios.

facts.statement: It is also believed that heterodontosauriforms may have given rise to marginocephalians, which could explain the transitional characteristics of Yinlong.
facts.quote: Se cree también que los heterodontosauriformes pudieron dar origen a los marginocéfalos, lo que posiblemente explicaría las características transicionales del Yinlong.

facts.statement: This theory posits that Yinlong could be an evolutionary link between the two taxa and that the heterodontosaurian was effectively an ornithopod whose family was the link that gave rise to marginocephalians.
facts.quote: Esta teoría postula que el Yinlong puede ser un nexo evolutivo entre ambos taxones y que el heterodontosaurio efectivamente es un ornitópodo cuya familia fue el nexo que dio origen a los marginocéfalos.

facts.statement: Based on both theories, these dinosaurs are considered ceratopsians because their anatomy and physiology correspond to this group and diverge from ornithopods.
facts.quote: Por lo que demuestran ambas teorías, se considera a estos como ceratopsios, puesto que su anatomía y su fisiología corresponden a este grupo y se alejan de los ornitópodos.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus had a small but robust skull.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Heterodontosaurus era pequeño pero robusto.

facts.statement: The two most complete skulls measure 108 mm and 121 mm in length.
facts.quote: Los dos cráneos más completos miden 108 milímetros, el del espécimen holotipo SAM-PK-K337 y 121 milímetros el del espécimen SAM-PK-K1332, de longitud.

facts.statement: The genus name refers to the unusual heterodont dentition found in the skull, a trait usually associated with mammals.
facts.quote: Una característica inusual del cráneo fueron los dientes de forma diferente heterodoncia para los cuales se nombra el género, que de otra manera se conoce principalmente de los mamíferos.

facts.statement: Unlike most dinosaurs and reptiles which have one tooth type, Heterodontosaurus possessed three different types of teeth.
facts.quote: La mayoría de los dinosaurios y de hecho la mayoría de los reptiles tienen un solo tipo de diente en sus mandíbulas, pero Heterodontosaurus tenía tres.

facts.statement: The snout tip lacked teeth, while the posterior part of the upper premaxilla had three teeth on each side.
facts.quote: La punta de pico del hocico no tenía dientes, mientras que la parte posterior de la premaxilar en la mandíbula superior tenía tres dientes en cada lado.

facts.statement: The first two upper teeth were small and cone-shaped like incisors, while the third on each side was large and formed prominent tusk-like canines.
facts.quote: Los dos primeros dientes superiores eran pequeñas y en forma de cono, comparable a incisivos, mientras que el tercero en cada lado era mucho grande, formando prominentes, caninos tipo colmillos.

facts.statement: Eleven high, chisel-shaped molar teeth were aligned on each side of the posterior upper jaw, separated from the canines by a large gap.
facts.quote: Once dientes molares altos y con forma de cincel se alinearon a cada lado de las partes posteriores de la mandíbula superior, que se separaron de los caninos por un gran diastema.

facts.statement: The front of the jaws was covered by a toothless keratinous beak or rhamphotheca.
facts.quote: La parte frontal de las mandíbulas estaba cubierta por un pico queratínico sin dientes o rhamphotheca.

facts.statement: The jugal bone formed a "blade" that created a groove with a tab on the pterygoid bone to guide the movement of the lower jaw.
facts.quote: El hueso yugal también formó una "cuchilla" que creó una ranura junto con una pestaña en el hueso pterigoideo, para guiar el movimiento de la mandíbula inferior.

facts.statement: The left and right upper temporal fossae were separated by the sagittal crest, which likely provided lateral attachment surfaces for jaw muscles in the living animal.
facts.quote: Las fosas temporales superiores izquierda y derecha estaban separadas por la cresta sagital, que habría proporcionado superficies de unión laterales para la musculatura de la mandíbula en el animal vivo.

facts.statement: In the juvenile skull SAM-PK-K10487, the eye sockets became proportionally smaller as the animal grew, while the snout became longer and contained additional teeth.
facts.quote: Como lo muestra el cráneo juvenil SAM-PK-K10487, las cuencas de los ojos se hicieron proporcionalmente más pequeñas a medida que el animal crecía, y el hocico se hizo más largo y contenía dientes adicionales.

facts.statement: The juvenile skull length was suggested to be 45 mm.
facts.quote: Se sugirió que la longitud del cráneo juvenil era de 45 milímetros.

facts.statement: Assuming body proportions similar to adults, the juvenile's body length would have been 450 mm.
facts.quote: Suponiendo proporciones corporales similares a las de los adultos, la longitud corporal de este juvenil habría sido de 450 milímetros.

facts.statement: The teeth had a thick enamel layer on the inner side, were adapted for wear (hypsodonty), and had long roots firmly embedded in their sockets.
facts.quote: Estos dientes tenían una capa gruesa de esmalte en el lado interno y estaban adaptados para el desgaste, hipsodoncia y tenían largas raíces, firmemente incrustadas en sus cuencas.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus belongs to the parent group Heterodontosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Heterodontosaurinae

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus is classified in the family Heterodontosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Heterodontosauridae

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurus is a member of the class Ornithischia.
